activities.subject: reading
activities.title: Sound Seeds: s a t p

learn.text: Letters make sounds. s says ssss like a snake. a says a like in apple. t says t like a ticking clock. p says p like popping bubbles.
learn.say: Letters make sounds. S says sss, like a snake. A says a, like apple. T says t, like a tick. P says p, like pop!

lines.text: S is for snake, and the snake says sss.
A is for apple, crunch, a, a, a.
T is for tiger, t, t, t.
P is for pig, p, p, p.
S, a, t, p, sing the sounds with me!

misconceptions.description: Uses the letter name (e.g. 'ess') instead of the sound ('sss').
misconceptions.remedy: We say the sound, not the name: s is 'sss', like a snake.

misconceptions.description: Confuses sounds that are made in a similar way (e.g. p and b, t and d).
misconceptions.remedy: Put your hand in front of your mouth. p makes a little puff of air.

items.prompt: Snake starts with sss. Which letter says sss?
items.say: Snake. Ssssnake. Which letter says sss?
hints: It looks like a wiggly snake!
items.explanation: s says sss, like the start of snake.

items.prompt: Which letter does apple start with?
items.say: Apple. A, a, apple. Which letter?
items.explanation: Apple starts with the a sound.

items.prompt: Which letter does tiger start with?
items.say: Tiger. T, t, tiger.
hints: Listen to the first sound: t-iger.
It sounds like a clock: t, t, t.
items.explanation: Tiger starts with t.

items.prompt: Which letter does pig start with?
items.say: Pig. P, p, pig.
hints: Feel the little puff of air: p.
items.explanation: Pig starts with p. Feel the puff of air!

items.prompt: Which picture starts with s?
items.say: Which picture starts with sss?
items.explanation: Sun starts with sss.

items.prompt: Which picture starts with t?
items.say: Which picture starts with t?
hints: Ant ends with t, but how does it start?
items.explanation: Tent starts with t. Ant has a t sound at the end, not the start.

activities.subject: reading
activities.title: Sound Seeds: i n m d

learn.text: Four new sounds! i like in insect. n like a buzzing nnn. m like mmm, yummy! d like a drum: d, d, d.
learn.say: Four new sounds! I, like insect. Nnn, like net. Mmm, like yummy. D, like drum.

misconceptions.description: Mixes up m and n, which look and sound alike.
misconceptions.remedy: m has two humps and you close your lips: mmm. n has one hump and your lips stay open: nnn.
d: the round part comes first, then the line, like a drum and a drumstick.

items.prompt: Which letter does moon start with?
items.say: Moon. Mmm, moon.
hints: Close your lips and hum: mmm.
items.explanation: Moon starts with m. Lips together: mmm.

items.prompt: Which letter does dog start with?
items.say: Dog. D, d, dog.
hints: Tap your tongue behind your teeth: d.
items.explanation: Dog starts with d, like a drum beat.

items.prompt: Which letter does nest start with?
items.say: Nest. Nnn, nest.
items.explanation: Nest starts with n. Lips open: nnn.

items.prompt: Which letter does insect start with?
items.say: Insect. I, i, insect.
hints: It's a short sound, like the start of 'itchy'.
items.explanation: Insect starts with i.

items.prompt: Which picture starts with m?
items.explanation: Mouse starts with m.

items.prompt: Which word starts with d?
hints: d has its round part first, then the line.
items.explanation: dig starts with d. big starts with b, which looks like d turned round.

learn.text: Every word starts with a sound. Say the word slowly and listen to the very first sound. Ball starts with b!
learn.say: Every word starts with a sound. Say the word slowly. Ball. B, ball.

misconceptions.description: Picks the last sound of the word instead of the first.
misconceptions.remedy: Listen to the very beginning of the word.

misconceptions.description: Matches by meaning (e.g. cat with dog) rather than by sound.
misconceptions.remedy: We are listening to sounds, not thinking about what the words mean.

items.prompt: Which one starts the same as bear?
items.say: Bear. Which one starts with the same sound as bear?
items.explanation: Bear and bus both start with b.

items.prompt: Which one starts the same as fish?
items.say: Fish. Which one starts like fish?
items.explanation: Fish and frog both start with f.

items.prompt: Which one does NOT start with r?
items.say: Rabbit, rain, lemon. Which one does not start with r?
hints: Say each word. Listen for rrr.
items.explanation: Rabbit and rain start with r. Lemon starts with l.

items.prompt: Goat starts with...
items.say: Goat. What sound does goat start with?
items.explanation: Goat starts with g. The t sound is at the end.

items.prompt: Which two start with the same sound?
items.say: Which two start with the same sound?
hints: Listen to the start of each word, not the end.
items.explanation: Hat and hen both start with h. Hat and cat sound the same at the end, which is a rhyme.

items.prompt: Wolf starts with...
items.say: Wolf. What sound does wolf start with?
items.explanation: Wolf starts with w.

learn.text: Rhyming words sound the same at the end. Cat, hat and bat all end in 'at'. They rhyme!
learn.say: Rhyming words sound the same at the end. Cat, hat, bat. They all rhyme!

lines.text: A cat in a hat sat down on a mat.
A frog on a log met a dog in the fog.
A bee in a tree looked down at me.
Rhymes sound the same at the end, you see!

misconceptions.description: Picks a word with the same first sound rather than the same ending.
misconceptions.remedy: Rhymes match at the end of the word, not the start.

misconceptions.description: Picks a word with a related meaning.
misconceptions.remedy: Listen to how the word sounds, not what it means.

items.prompt: What rhymes with cat?
items.say: Cat. What rhymes with cat?
items.explanation: Cat and hat both end in 'at'.

items.prompt: What rhymes with bee?
items.say: Bee. What rhymes with bee?
items.explanation: Bee and tree both end in 'ee'.

items.prompt: What rhymes with snake?
items.say: Snake. What rhymes with snake?
items.explanation: Snake and cake both end in 'ake'.

items.prompt: Which one does NOT rhyme? log, frog, sun
items.say: Log, frog, sun. Which one does not rhyme?
hints: Which one has a different ending?
items.explanation: Log and frog rhyme. Sun ends in 'un', so it doesn't rhyme with them.

items.prompt: Finish the rhyme: The fox sat in a ...
items.say: Finish the rhyme. The fox sat in a...
items.explanation: Fox and box rhyme.

items.prompt: Which pair rhymes?
items.say: Which pair of words rhyme?
hints: Listen to the ends of the words.
items.explanation: Moon and spoon both end in 'oon'. Moon and mouse only start the same.

learn.text: To read a word, say each sound, then push them together fast. s - a - t ... sat! This is called blending.
learn.say: To read a word, say each sound, then push them together. S, a, t. Sat!

misconceptions.description: Reads the first sound then guesses a word.
misconceptions.remedy: Say every sound, all the way to the end.

misconceptions.description: Reads the middle vowel wrongly (e.g. pin for pan).
misconceptions.remedy: Look carefully at the middle letter and say its sound.

items.prompt: s - a - t. Which picture?
items.say: S. A. T. Push the sounds together.
hints: Say each sound, then say them faster.
items.explanation: s, a, t blends to make sat, like sitting on a chair.

items.prompt: Read the word: pin
items.say: P. I. N. What does it say?
items.explanation: p, i, n blends to pin.

items.prompt: Read the word and pick the picture.
items.say: Read the word, then pick the picture.
items.explanation: m, a, p makes map.

items.prompt: Read the word and pick the picture.
items.explanation: d, i, g blends to dig.

items.prompt: Build the word 'tap'.
items.say: Build the word tap. T, a, p.
hints: What is the first sound in tap?
items.explanation: t, a, p makes tap.

items.prompt: Build the word 'man'.
items.say: Build the word man. M, a, n.
hints: Lips together for the first sound.
items.explanation: m, a, n makes man.

learn.text: Listen to the story. Think about who is in it, where they are and what happens.

visual.title: The Lost Kite
visual.text: Zara had a red kite. She went to the park with Grandpa. The wind blew and blew. Whoosh! The kite flew up into a tall tree. Grandpa got a long stick. He tapped the branch, and the kite fell down. Zara gave Grandpa a big hug.

learn.say: Zara had a red kite. She went to the park with Grandpa. The wind blew and blew. Whoosh! The kite flew up into a tall tree. Grandpa got a long stick. He tapped the branch, and the kite fell down. Zara gave Grandpa a big hug.

misconceptions.description: Picks something that sounds likely but was not in the story.
misconceptions.remedy: Think back: what did the story actually say?

misconceptions.description: Remembers the event but confuses a detail.
misconceptions.remedy: Listen to the story again and look for that part.

items.prompt: What colour was Zara's kite?
items.say: What colour was Zara's kite?
hints: Think about the very first sentence.
items.explanation: The story says: Zara had a red kite.

items.prompt: Who went to the park with Zara?
items.say: Who went to the park with Zara?
hints: She went to the park with...
Who did she hug at the end?
items.explanation: Zara went to the park with Grandpa.

items.prompt: Where did the kite get stuck?
items.say: Where did the kite get stuck?
hints: Whoosh! The kite flew up into a...
items.explanation: The kite flew up into a tall tree.

items.prompt: What made the kite fly away?
items.say: What made the kite fly away?
items.explanation: The wind blew and blew, and the kite flew away.

items.prompt: Put the story in order.
items.say: Put the story in order. What happened first?
hints: What happened at the very start?
The hug was at the end.
items.explanation: First they went to the park, then the kite got stuck, and at the end Zara hugged Grandpa.

items.prompt: How do you think Zara felt at the end?
items.say: How do you think Zara felt at the end?
items.explanation: Zara got her kite back and gave Grandpa a big hug, so she felt happy and thankful.
